problem: Cloud spend was high relative to a stable, predictable workload.
title: 37signals leaves the public cloud for owned hardware
context: 37signals ran Basecamp and HEY on public cloud services with large monthly bills.
decision_made: Move applications off the public cloud to hardware the company owns.
action_taken: Migrated apps and later reported on the savings.
observed_outcome: By Sept 2023 cloud spend excluding S3 was reported down about 60 percent; hardware cost of about $700,000 was recouped during 2023. Later projections raised savings to over $10 million over five years.
lessons: Predictable, steady workloads with in-house operations skill may cost less on owned hardware.
limitations: Self-reported by the company that made the choice. Depends on having a capable ops team and stable demand, which many companies lack. Projections are not results.

claims.claim_text: 37signals moved its applications off the public cloud.
Cloud spend excluding S3 was reported down about 60 percent, from about $180,000 to under $80,000 per month.
